source.context: Chapter 7 section 7.4, Example 12 (preceding PDF page150/printed158): compact products of I=[0,1] and the circle C.

mathematics: The graphic uses the factor order I×C, matching its boundary-fiber labels; the preceding prose also names the homeomorphic product C×I.
The top and bottom fibers are {1}×C and {0}×C, and the marked side fiber is I×{x}.
Both factor topologies and the product topology are declared compact; fibers are compact subsets of the product.
The representative x is checked against the circle equation; native render tests verify its projected point lies exactly on the upper ellipse.
visualFidelity: One cylinder panel, full solid top and bottom ellipses, upright side edges and all five source labels are preserved.
The two upper marked points, right endpoint numerals and left interval-fiber label follow the source composition.
Only the lateral surface receives restrained orange shading; the endpoint openings stay white.
The source intentionally exposes the full lower ellipse. The view preserves this wireframe occlusion convention, rather than hiding its far arc.
figures.comparison: Viewed the source graphic and native SVG side by side at the same graphic width after reducing canvas padding and matching lettering scale.
limitations: The scanned contours are slightly irregular; the native ellipses are exact.

source.context: Chapter 7 section 7.4, Example 12: the compact product I³.

mathematics: The cube is the iterated product (I×I)×I; its topology is the iterated product of compact interval topologies.
The marked left face fixes the first coordinate to zero: {0}×I×I. The marked top face fixes the third coordinate to one: I×I×{1}.
Both faces are asserted compact subsets of the cube, and the lower/upper endpoint singletons preserve the closed interval boundaries.
visualFidelity: One cube panel with all twelve solid wireframe edges and its original oblique projection is preserved.
The left face has dense vertical hatching; the top has diagonal hatching and the source’s additional vertical crosshatching near its back vertex.
The bent leader points left into the first-coordinate-zero face, matching the source arrow direction.
Both face labels have white knockouts; the 0 and 1 numerals remain at the front left vertical edge.
Pale orange fill is confined to the two marked faces.
figures.comparison: Viewed the source graphic and native SVG side by side at the same graphic width, including an enlarged source crop to confirm the leader and crosshatching.
limitations: The source uses slightly nonparallel scanned edges; the view uses an affine oblique projection.
Annotation dragging changes layout while the compact product and boundary-face geometry stay fixed.
